title: GitHub Copilot for Enterprise C# & .NET Development
description: Maximize developer productivity in Visual Studio and VS Code with GitHub Copilot Chat, multi-file edits, and custom repository instructions.

data.text: GitHub Copilot has transformed modern software engineering from typing every line of boilerplate code by hand to pair programming with an intelligent context-aware assistant. For .NET developers working in Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code, Copilot offers three distinct interaction modes: inline code completions, interactive Copilot Chat, and multi-file Copilot Edits. Using Copilot effectively requires mastering contextual prompts, steering the model with domain conventions, and reviewing generated code critically.

To prevent Copilot from generating outdated C# patterns or proposing deprecated libraries, create a .github/copilot-instructions.md file at the root of your repository. Copilot automatically loads these instructions into its system prompt context for every developer on your team.

data.title: Production .github/copilot-instructions.md for .NET 9 Teams
data.content: Specifies C# 13 and .NET 9 coding standards for GitHub Copilot:
data.code:
# Enterprise .NET 9 & C# 13 Team Standards for GitHub Copilot

## Language & Framework Guidelines
- Always target .NET 9 and C# 13 features.
- Prefer primary constructors for dependency injection in classes.
- Use strongly-typed records for DTOs and value objects.
- Avoid legacy patterns: never suggest `ArrayList`, `Hashtable`, or blocking `.Result` / `.Wait()`.

## Architecture & Resiliency
- Always accept `CancellationToken` in asynchronous methods.
- When building HTTP clients, use `IHttpClientFactory` and Polly v8 resilience pipelines.
- Use `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` interfaces (`IChatClient`, `IEmbeddingGenerator`) instead of raw SDK types.
- For structured logging, use compile-time `[LoggerMessage]` source generators.

## Testing Guidelines
- Write unit tests using xUnit, FluentAssertions, and Moq.
- Name test methods using the pattern: `MethodName_StateUnderTest_ExpectedBehavior`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GitHub Copilot boosts .NET developer velocity across completions, chat, and multi-file edits
Codify team coding standards in .github/copilot-instructions.md to ensure modern C# 13 patterns
Use chat participants (@workspace, #file, @terminal) to provide precise local context
Leverage Copilot to accelerate unit test authoring, LINQ queries, and regex generation
Never commit AI-generated code without peer code review, unit tests, and security scrutiny
data.takeaway: GitHub Copilot is a powerful co-pilot, but the human engineer remains the pilot in command. Guiding Copilot with repository instructions and contextual tags yields high-quality, idiomatic .NET code.
